# The overpayment again, this time naming the parked split outright.
#
# The sibling spelling — `txn_guid:` alone — refuses this, and its refusal ends
# "name the settling one with `txn_split_guid:`". So this is the very edit a
# reader is sent to make, and it has to be refused for the same reason rather
# than quietly doing what the other spelling would not.
#
# Measured before that: naming the split, every guard passed — not in a lot,
# bank present, bank USD like the receivable, only two splits — and the run
# wrote −120.00 USD onto the receivable and put it in the lot. The lot came to
# 100 − 120 = −20: the invoice read paid, the customer's 20.00 was in no credit
# lot, and nothing disagreed. Exit 0.
#
# What this fixture produces: the same refusal `txn_guid:` alone earns.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-02
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "0718293a4b5c6d7e8f90011223344556"
    txn_split_guid: "8293a4b5c6d7e8f900112233445566aa"
